:::{#def-big-o}
#### Big-O notation

Let $f$ and $g$ be functions from the positive integers to $[0, \infty)$.
We write $f(n) = O(g(n))$ if there are a constant $c > 0$
and an integer $n_0$ such that

$$f(n) \le c \, g(n) \quad \text{for every } n \ge n_0.$$

That is, $f$ grows no faster than a constant multiple of $g$
once $n$ is large enough.
This is the definition of @arora2009computational [section 0.3].

:::
